name: Feedback activity management
description: Setting up a Feedback activity: creating and configuring the survey, writing its questions of every type, ordering them into pages, and making questions conditional on earlier answers.
instructions:
Build a feedback in order: create the activity, then add its questions, which are stored separately from its settings. Read current state first with x_mod_feedback_pre_update, which returns the settings and the questions together.

Decide anonymous before anyone answers. Switching it afterwards leaves the responses already given as they were, so the results mix named and anonymous sets, and an info question stamping the response time works only while responses are named. With autonumbering on, which is the default, do not number the questions yourself in their text.

Choosing a question type by what you want back:
- One answer from a short list, shown as buttons: multichoice with subtype radio. A radio question offers a 'Not selected' choice on top of your options unless hidenoselect is 1. When the question is required, set hidenoselect to 1: the choice cannot be submitted anyway, so leaving it on adds a dead first option and, being the default, it is the one already filled in.
- One answer from a long list, shown as a dropdown: multichoice with subtype dropdown.
- Several answers at once: multichoice with subtype check.
- A rating you want an average of: multichoicerated, whose options each carry a number. A plain multichoice cannot be averaged, so a satisfaction scale should almost always be multichoicerated. Respondents read the score printed in front of each option with no space surviving between the two, so a label of Very satisfied comes out as (4)Very satisfied. Option text accepts HTML, so start every label with   and it reads as (4) Very satisfied instead. Score the best answer highest and the worst lowest, since nothing in Moodle knows which way your scale runs and it simply averages the numbers, so an inverted scale gives a high average to an unhappy cohort. Never repeat the score in the wording: values 1 to 5 against labels 1 to 5 come out as (1)1 (2)2. Where the numbers should not be visible at all, only a plain multichoice can hide them, and then there is no average.
- A number, optionally bounded: numeric.
- A sentence or two of free text: textfield. A paragraph or more: textarea.
- A heading or an explanation sitting between questions, asking nothing: label.
- The course, the course category or the time of the response, recorded alongside the answers without asking anything: info.
- A check that the respondent is a person: captcha.

Order and pages. A page break is an item with a position of its own, so positions count them. Moving one question is a position on x_mod_feedback_update_item. Reordering a whole feedback is one call to mod_feedback_questions_reorder instead, which takes the course module id and the complete list of item ids. For a brand new feedback, list the questions in final order and leave position out of all of them.

Conditional questions need four things together: dependitem naming an earlier question that collects an answer, dependvalue holding the answer that reveals this one, a page break somewhere between the two, and a label on the earlier question. The page break is not decoration: Moodle can only act on an answer the respondent has already submitted, and it hides a conditional question from everyone when the break is missing. The label is what the edit form lists the possible targets by, and it leaves out every question that has none, so without one the condition is invisible in the browser and opening the dependent question and saving it drops the condition. dependvalue is matched against the stored option text character for character, so when the target is a multichoicerated question whose labels start with   the dependvalue has to start with it too:  Dissatisfied, not Dissatisfied.

Worked example, a survey that asks for detail only from unhappy respondents. Add, in this order: a multichoicerated question "How satisfied are you with the course?" with the label satisfaction, needed because the next question depends on it, and the options  Very satisfied worth 4,  Satisfied 3,  Neutral 2 and  Dissatisfied 1; then a pagebreak; then a textfield question "What should we change?" whose dependitem is the first question and whose dependvalue is  Dissatisfied, matching that option's stored text. Everyone answers the rating on page one; only those who chose Dissatisfied are shown the follow up on page two, and everyone else finishes there.

What to watch for:
- Editing or deleting a question on a feedback that already has responses destroys the answers given to it, with no undo. x_mod_feedback_pre_update reports has_responses; read the results with mod_feedback_get_analysis before changing anything.
- Whether a respondent may answer more than once is frozen the moment the first response arrives.
- A page break cannot be the first item, and two cannot sit at the end.

Naming. A question's name is the wording the respondent reads, so write it as a question. The label is a separate short tag for the teacher, such as Q1 or satisfaction: it becomes the column heading in the results table and in exports, and prefixes the question on the edit and analysis pages, but respondents never see it. Leave it out. Almost no feedback needs labels, and one invented for a question that was perfectly clear without it only adds clutter to the edit page. Set a label only when the teacher asks for one, when another question depends on this one, or when they ask for something that needs it, such as particular column headings in an export.
